messages.content: You are a helpful assistant experienced in museum and informal science education operations, supporting a director relaunching a planetarium's dome shows.

Hi, Cedarholm Planetarium is relaunching after years of running the same tired dome show on aging equipment. We're upgrading the projector system, writing a brand-new original show, revamping our school field trip program, redoing membership tiers, and throwing a fundraising gala to help pay for it all. I'd like to plan the whole relaunch with you.
Good question. The honest answer is it depends on your scale, but I'd start conservative and tighten as you learn. Want me to sketch a rough default?
Let's start with the projector and dome system. Our current setup is a single-channel analog star projector from the 90s. What should I be weighing when picking a full-dome digital replacement?
Short version: aim for the simplest approach that still gives you a safety margin, then revisit once you have real data. Happy to go deeper.

Projector decision. Three finalists: (1) a top-tier dual 4K laser projection system from the industry leader, (2) a mid-range single-projector fisheye system from a smaller vendor at half the cost, or (3) refurbishing our existing analog star ball with a digital overlay add-on. The board approved option two, the mid-range single-projector fisheye system, to stretch the budget toward the show script and gala.
Got it, noted, and I'll keep that in mind as we keep planning.
For the new show script, how long should a resident dome show typically run for a mixed family audience, versus something aimed more at adults?
Good question. The honest answer is it depends on your scale, but I'd start conservative and tighten as you learn. Want me to sketch a rough default?

Terminology note: 'the show' is overloaded right now. Some staff use 'the show' loosely for whatever licensed traveling program we're currently screening, but when I say the show to you, I always mean our new original resident show that we're writing in-house. That's the sense I want.
Understood. I've locked that in on my end.
On school field trips, how far in advance do teachers typically need to book a planetarium slot for it to fit their curriculum planning?
Short version: aim for the simplest approach that still gives you a safety margin, then revisit once you have real data. Happy to go deeper.

Hard rule for the relaunch: no sponsor logos or ads displayed during the dome show itself, before, during, or after. Sponsors can be thanked in the lobby and printed program, but the dome experience stays commercial-free no matter how much a sponsor offers to pay for a pre-show slide.
Thanks for the clarity, that's noted going forward.
Membership question: should we offer a single flat membership tier, or multiple tiers based on visit frequency?
There's a sensible middle ground here. I'd avoid over-engineering it this early and set a baseline you can adjust. Let me know if you want specifics.

For the record on licensed content: we tried a licensed show package from a vendor called SkyDome Media two seasons ago, and it had visible rendering artifacts and banding on our old projector that families complained about even before this upgrade. We're not licensing from them again.
Makes sense. I'll factor that into everything else we work through.
For the gala, what's a realistic per-ticket price for a first-time fundraising event at a mid-size regional planetarium?
Reasonable to plan for this now. A light-touch process usually beats a heavy one at your stage. I can outline one if that helps.

Random note to park here: the new projector's install and commissioning is scheduled to complete on the 9th, and the unit's serial number is PJ-58820 for our warranty records. Nothing to decide, just don't want to lose track of it.
Noted, and I'll respect that as we go.
Back to the projector, how disruptive is the installation process, in terms of how long the dome would need to be closed to the public?
I'd treat that as a judgment call anchored to your actual constraints rather than a fixed rule. Want me to walk through the tradeoffs?

Let's codename the master dome control console 'Palpatine' from now on. Every internal doc and vendor ticket should say Palpatine instead of the real system name, since we sometimes discuss its quirks in shared docs with outside contractors.
Good to have that on the record. I'll carry it forward.

Narration decision for the new show. Three options: (1) hire a professional voice actor for a fully pre-recorded track, (2) keep live narration performed by staff at every showing, or (3) a hybrid with pre-recorded narration but a live host doing intro and Q&A. We're going with the hybrid, pre-recorded narration plus a live host.
Got it, noted, and I'll keep that in mind as we keep planning.
For the show script, should the narration be pre-recorded, or should we keep doing live narration like we do now?
Fair thing to nail down. Keep it proportional to your resources and don't gold-plate it yet. I can suggest a starting point.

Also, when I say 'members' from here on I mean people on our individual annual membership tier specifically, not the broader family membership tier. I know staff sometimes say 'members' to mean anyone with any kind of membership, but with you, members means the individual tier.
Understood. I've locked that in on my end.
On field trips, what's a reasonable group size cap per session before the experience starts to suffer?
That one rewards a bit of upfront planning. Set a clear default, document it, and stay flexible. Glad to expand.

Another hard line: student field trip admission stays free, permanently, regardless of the gala's fundraising results or any budget shortfall. We will cut other things before we ever start charging schools for field trips.
Thanks for the clarity, that's noted going forward.
Membership again, should family memberships include unlimited free dome show admission, or a capped number of visits per year?
Good question. The honest answer is it depends on your scale, but I'd start conservative and tighten as you learn. Want me to sketch a rough default?

Also worth noting: we tried an all-volunteer narrator program for a few months last year, rotating through six different volunteers. Quality was wildly inconsistent, some sessions ran long, others rushed through the material. We're not going back to that model.
Makes sense. I'll factor that into everything else we work through.
One of our part-time staff, Alicia, has turned out to be a genuinely gifted live narrator. I want to make sure the new show plays to that strength.
Short version: aim for the simplest approach that still gives you a safety margin, then revisit once you have real data. Happy to go deeper.
Fundraising note for my own records: the gala's target is $75,000, with the date set for the second Saturday of next month. Just parking that here.
Noted, and I'll respect that as we go.
For the gala, should it double as a members-only preview of the new show, or stay a separate event entirely?
There's a sensible middle ground here. I'd avoid over-engineering it this early and set a baseline you can adjust. Let me know if you want specifics.
Let's call our senior volunteer docent trainer 'Gandalf' in all future notes. It's just quicker to type than his full title every time we talk about scheduling him for training sessions.
Good to have that on the record. I'll carry it forward.
Back to the projector install, what should our contingency plan be if it slips past our planned reopening date?
Good question. The honest answer is it depends on your scale, but I'd start conservative and tighten as you learn. Want me to sketch a rough default?
On the projector system we're getting, no need to recap the alternatives, what's the expected install timeline once it ships?
Short version: aim for the simplest approach that still gives you a safety margin, then revisit once you have real data. Happy to go deeper.
For the narration approach we picked, don't walk through the options again, how much studio time should we budget to record the pre-recorded portion?
There's a sensible middle ground here. I'd avoid over-engineering it this early and set a baseline you can adjust. Let me know if you want specifics.
Is the show's script tight enough to start blocking camera movements for the dome yet?
Reasonable to plan for this now. A light-touch process usually beats a heavy one at your stage. I can outline one if that helps.
How many members should we expect to renew before the gala invitations need to go out?
I'd treat that as a judgment call anchored to your actual constraints rather than a fixed rule. Want me to walk through the tradeoffs?
Is Palpatine reliable enough to trust for the gala preview, or should we keep a manual backup plan ready?
Fair thing to nail down. Keep it proportional to your resources and don't gold-plate it yet. I can suggest a starting point.
Can you draft a short thank-you note to Gandalf for covering last week's field trip overflow?
That one rewards a bit of upfront planning. Set a clear default, document it, and stay flexible. Glad to expand.
For field trips, should we require a minimum group size to book a session, or accept any size?
Good question. The honest answer is it depends on your scale, but I'd start conservative and tighten as you learn. Want me to sketch a rough default?
